text: Every day, your heart beats about one hundred thousand times, and pumps around seven thousand liters of blood through your body. So how does one small muscle do all that? Let's follow the blood on its journey through the heart.

Your heart sits in the middle of your chest, between your two lungs, tilted slightly to the left. It's about the size of your fist, and it's made of a special muscle, called cardiac muscle, that keeps working your whole life without tiring out.

Inside, the heart is really two pumps, side by side, separated by a wall called the septum. Each side has two chambers. An upper chamber, the atrium, receives blood. A lower chamber, the ventricle, pumps blood out. That gives us four chambers: the right atrium, the right ventricle, the left atrium, and the left ventricle.

To keep blood moving in one direction, the heart has four valves that work like one way doors. The tricuspid valve and the pulmonary valve are on the right side. The mitral valve and the aortic valve are on the left side.

Now let's follow the blood. Oxygen poor blood from the body returns through two large veins, the superior and inferior vena cava, into the right atrium. It passes through the tricuspid valve into the right ventricle, which pumps it through the pulmonary valve into the pulmonary artery, and on to the lungs.
In the lungs, the blood drops off carbon dioxide and picks up fresh oxygen. Now full of oxygen, it travels back to the heart through the pulmonary veins, into the left atrium.

From the left atrium, blood passes through the mitral valve into the left ventricle. This is the strongest chamber, with the thickest wall, because it has to push blood to your entire body. It pumps the blood through the aortic valve into the aorta, the largest artery in the body, and out to every organ.

And that famous heartbeat sound, lub dub? That's the valves closing. Lub is the tricuspid and mitral valves shutting, as the ventricles start to squeeze. Dub is the pulmonary and aortic valves shutting, as the ventricles relax.

So, to sum up. The right side of the heart sends blood to the lungs to pick up oxygen. The left side sends that oxygen rich blood to the whole body. And four valves keep it all flowing in one direction. In the next video, we'll look at the heart's electrical system, and how it keeps this rhythm going.
